perspective:
Vincent’s available information:

- He knows Patrick Guzman as a long-time friend from their teenage years; they are both blue-collar workers and have collaborated, with Vincent contributing mechanical skills and Patrick construction expertise.
- At the diner, Vincent knows Patrick is considering a new construction venture/investment to expand Patrick’s business. Patrick told him it seems like a good opportunity. Vincent told Patrick he had heard it was risky and asked if he was sure. Patrick said he thought it was worth the risk but was still weighing options. Vincent expressed worry about financial security and suggested reconsidering or delaying until more information was gathered. Patrick thanked him and said he would think it over.
- Over the next few days, Vincent noticed Patrick avoiding detailed discussions about the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent said they needed to talk and that he felt Patrick was not telling him everything. Patrick said it was complicated and he had not wanted to worry Vincent with details. Vincent said that was exactly why they needed to discuss it, and that as a friend he felt betrayed by the lack of transparency. Patrick apologized, said he should have been more open, and offered to sit down and explain everything.
- At Vincent’s garage, during their detailed discussion, Vincent learned the investment troubles were serious. Patrick told him it had been tough and that he might lose a significant amount if it did not turn around soon. Vincent offered to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick thanked him and said he was grateful for the support.
- A month later at the coffee shop, Vincent had information suggesting the venture might actually turn a profit. He said this to Patrick. Patrick said it was starting to look up and he was relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologized for doubting him earlier and proposed a joint venture, saying he saw potential. Patrick agreed and said they should work out the details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent and Patrick were optimistic about the joint venture. Vincent said their combined skills could make it a success. Patrick said he was excited. Vincent said they should start the business plan and outline every step carefully. Patrick agreed they should cover all bases and set it up for success.
- Vincent knows his own statements, feelings, and actions in these interactions—such as worry, feeling betrayed, apologizing, offering a loan, and proposing the joint venture—and he heard Patrick’s statements and observed Patrick’s actions during their meetings. He has no access to hidden events, private thoughts, or information not stated or observed by him.
